body.statement: For every \((\theta_{dj})\in\mathcal T_K(r)\), the sharp lower bound on \(\mathbb E|Y(1)-Y(0)|\) over couplings preserving the two conditional Bernoulli laws cell by cell is \(L_K\), and \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\).
body.justification: This setup proposition fixes the actual causal partial-identification endpoint before any statistical approximation and provides a sanity check for the collision parameterization.
body.gap: This identity is a direct binary specialization of Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's general sharp COT bound in Theorem~1; no novelty is claimed for the affine calculation.
body.consumer: The identity lets \(\texttt{causalPIviaCOT}\) interpret partition-resolution diagnostics directly as uncertainty about a sharp endpoint rather than about an auxiliary regression coefficient.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an array in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\), and let \(P_\theta\) denote the observable law of \(\mathcal O_K\) induced by the uniform cell probabilities and the conditional Bernoulli probabilities \(p_{dj}\).  A compatible causal law is obtained by choosing, separately in every cell \(j\), a coupling \(\pi_j\) of \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{0j})\) and \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{1j})\).  Thus, for the causal mismatch parameter
\[
 \tau(\pi)=\frac1K\sum_{j=1}^K
 \Pr_{\pi_j}\{Y(1)\ne Y(0)\},
\]
the identified set is
\[
 \Theta_I(P_\theta)=
 \left\{
 \frac1K\sum_{j=1}^K t_j:
 |p_{1j}-p_{0j}|\le t_j\le
 \min\{p_{0j}+p_{1j},,2-p_{0j}-p_{1j}\}
 \right\}.
\]
Indeed, if \(Q_j=\Pr_{\pi_j}\{Y(0)=Y(1)=1\}\), then
\[
 \Pr_{\pi_j}\{Y(1)\ne Y(0)\}=p_{0j}+p_{1j}-2Q_j,
\]
and the elementary nonnegativity constraints on the four binary atoms give
\[
 \max\{0,p_{0j}+p_{1j}-1\}\le Q_j\le\min\{p_{0j},p_{1j}\}.
\]
Conversely, every \(Q_j\) in this interval defines four nonnegative atoms with the prescribed marginals.  Hence the displayed cellwise interval, and therefore the displayed identified set, is sharp.  This is the binary extremal-coupling technique; in particular its lower endpoint is the observed-law functional
\[
 L_K=\frac1K\sum_{j=1}^K|p_{1j}-p_{0j}|.
\]
By the amplitude ordering and the sign restriction,
\[
 |p_{1j}-p_{0j}|=|b\theta_{1j}-a\theta_{0j}|
 =\begin{cases}
 a-b,&\theta_{0j}\theta_{1j}=1,\\
 a+b,&\theta_{0j}\theta_{1j}=-1,
 \end{cases}
 =a-b\theta_{0j}\theta_{1j}.
\]
Averaging and using the definition of \(\rho_K\) yields \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\).  Thus the equality between the causal sharp endpoint and the observed-law functional has been proved from the coupling constraints rather than imposed as a definition.
